title: Lattiq
description: A local-first writing room with a working editor, readable device-only saving and separately documented collaboration experiments.
status: Unreleased local d7071fe: device-only editor, reload persistence and formatting verified; hosted collaboration was not exercised.

blocks.heading: The promise had to work
blocks.body: Lattiq puts a document on the device before it depends on a server. The current local writing-room pass checks the visible product: opening a scratch pad, editing and formatting a labelled synthetic sample, reloading it, and reading a shipped public-domain book. It runs with no WebSocket URL and accurately shows device-only storage. Earlier collaboration and benchmark evidence is kept separately below; this pass did not re-certify it.

blocks.heading: From the room to a saved page
blocks.body: The scratch pad opens through the writing-room navigation. A visibly labelled synthetic sample survived reload, and Heading 1 applied through the real toolbar became a heading in the document. Tabbing from Link reached the editable Document field; All documents returned to the room. On a 390px screen the eleven formatting buttons wrapped into two rows with at least 44px targets and no document overflow. These checks establish browser-local persistence and formatting, not a backup guarantee.

blocks.heading: A shelf that opens the actual editor
blocks.body: The reading-shelf link reaches the library section. Opening The Yellow Wallpaper loads its shipped public-domain text into the editable document. The shelf, room and editor share navigation and a restrained editorial palette. The shelf arrow is Lucide. No private library, account or remote storage was used.

blocks.body: The current d7071fe pass has normal lint, the 11 shared icon regressions and the production build with TypeScript passing; the final dependency audit reports zero findings. It does not re-certify collaboration, offline reconnect merging, older timing benchmarks or assistive-technology conformance. The captures are unreleased local views, not a deployment.

blocks.heading: Earlier collaboration repair: follow an edit across the stack

steps.label: Editor binding
steps.detail: Lexical’s CollaborationPlugin maps the visible document into Yjs. The document is loaded before network collaboration starts, and undo uses the collaborative history.

steps.label: Persistence and transport
steps.detail: The provider restores IndexedDB state and negotiates missing updates with Yjs state vectors. Heartbeats use a separate message type from presence.

steps.label: Room boundary
steps.detail: The server validates room names and optional expiring room tokens, owns socket presence, and writes room state through a temporary file and rename.

steps.label: Visible honesty
steps.detail: The status surface distinguishes device-only saving from collaboration. No WebSocket URL means the deployed editor stays local rather than showing pretend collaborators.

blocks.caption: The earlier release report verifies this collaboration path on localhost. The current writing-room pass used no room server. Hosted collaboration still needs a long-lived service with persistent storage.

blocks.heading: A protocol error disguised as a bundling problem
blocks.what: Collaboration had been removed after a lib0 decoder error, leaving a standalone editor without the promised sync.
blocks.why: The server answered a heartbeat with a byte the client interpreted as an awareness message, then tried to decode a payload that was not there. The report reproduces this without a bundler.
blocks.fix: Give heartbeat traffic its own message type, restore CollaborationPlugin inside LexicalCollaboration, and use Lexical’s own Yjs binding to build valid seeds.

blocks.heading: Persist the document, not an outgoing queue
blocks.context: An in-memory offline buffer disappears on reload. A convincing offline demo must survive closing and reopening the page.

options.label: Queue unsent messages in memory
options.detail: Works only while the tab stays alive.

options.label: Persist Yjs state in IndexedDB
options.detail: Load local state and apply the seed after the binding is ready, then connect and exchange missing state using Yjs state vectors.

blocks.outcome: Offline edits survive reload. A browser and server applying the same deterministic seed retain one copy. Undo follows the collaborative document rather than treating remote changes as local history.

blocks.heading: A bounded room server
blocks.body: The room server validates document names and can require expiring, room-scoped HMAC tokens. Presence belongs to a socket and is removed when it leaves. Disk writes use a temporary file and rename. This is a single-instance design with anonymous per-tab identities, not a multi-tenant permissions system.

blocks.heading: What those numbers establish
blocks.body: The earlier measurement report uses a production build and headless Chrome on an Apple M3, without network throttling. It measures that local code path, not the current writing-room pass or hosted internet latency. That report records two-way edits, presence removal, offline reload and convergence, seed deduplication, token rejection and console errors. The current device-only review did not start a room server or repeat those benchmarks.

The current local build runs device-only with an empty WebSocket URL. A hosted collaboration service would require a long-lived room server with persistent disk. Earlier local collaboration evidence is not a production service or a re-certification by the current room/editor/shelf pass.
